newsitem.title: USA: Columbia Gas sets Ohio rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Columbia Gas sets Ohio rate cut.

text.p: Columbia Gas of Ohio said Wednesday customers will see a reduction of about 13 percent in their bills beginning in April as the result of an early pass-through by the company of recent declines in the price of natural gas.
The move by the Columbia Gas System Inc subsidiary is pending approval by the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio.

According to Columbia chief executive Robert C. Skaggs Jr, the company was not scheduled to make its next natural gas cost adjustment until May, but asked regulators to approve a pass-through of the lower prices a month early.

"Columbia and other companies in Ohio and across the country were forced to pass on higher prices that resulted when abnormally cold weather at the beginning of the heating season pushed natural gas consumption up significantly," said Skaggs. "Since then, milder weather has caused consumption and prices to drop, and we have taken this action in order to pass the savings on to our customers as quickly as possible."
